Pause on N-surrogate for a complete
evidence reading of Experiment

N — Hybrid restart and precedence
surrogate. First, identify the

research question before looking at the
answer. The question asks

whether the fixed components create a
meaningful ordering surface, whether

a particular neighborhood provides useful
guidance on that surface, or

whether a cheaper executor is equally
effective. The sample is

5,040 orderings, and the source artifact
is

experiments/iteration-12/results/hybrid_surrogate.csv.
The horizontal axis

names the recorded independent
quantity—such as permutation size,

distance, or distinct evaluations. The
vertical axis names the measured

outcome—such as accuracy, error, hit
probability, regret, correlation, or

hitting time. Raw points remain visible
when their count permits.

A summary line or bar describes those
points; it does

not replace them. A capped observation
receives a censor marker,

and a sampled landscape never pretends to
be exhaustively enumerated.

The central pattern supports this finding:
Audited result reported in

the paper: precedence surrogate 14.8
[14,15] mean evaluations; elitist prism

54.2 [50,59]; random only 2/40 hits within
a 500-evaluation cap.

The correct limitation is: Audited result
reported in the paper:

precedence surrogate 14.8 [14,15] mean
evaluations; elitist prism 54.2

[50,59]; random only 2/40 hits within a
500-evaluation cap. That

limitation rules out a broader promotional
interpretation while preserving

the result actually measured. The decision
carried into the research

program is: Carry this constraint into the
next experiment and

compare methods at equal cost. Finally,
compare against the equal-budget

alternative. Generations, repeated cache
hits, and distinct evaluations are

not interchangeable. A method earns a
search-efficiency claim only when

uncertainty, evaluator resolution, optimum
density, and evaluation cost have
all been accounted for.
